I fixed it in `src/lru.py`. I haven't run the scenario or any tests.

`get` returned the value but never marked the key as recently used, so key 1 stayed first in the eviction order. In your scenario `put(3, 'c')` therefore evicted key 1 instead of key 2. `get` now moves the key to the most-recent end of `self.order` before returning, so `put(3, 'c')` evicts key 2 and `get(1)` returns `'a'`.

`order` is a list, so `get` and `put` are O(n) per call. If that matters, `collections.OrderedDict` would make them O(1). I left it alone since you only asked for the bug fix.
